prompt: In a right triangle, the side opposite angle $\theta$ has length $3$ and the hypotenuse has length $5$. What is the value of $\sin\theta$? Give your answer as a decimal.
hint: Each trigonometric ratio compares two particular sides of a right triangle. Which two sides does sine use?

hints.text: Each trigonometric ratio compares two particular sides of a right triangle. Which two sides does sine use?
Sine is the opposite side over the hypotenuse, so $\sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{5}$. Change that fraction into a decimal.

learningObjective: Compute a sine ratio in a right triangle.
explanation: The sine of an angle is the length of the opposite side divided by the length of the hypotenuse.
The opposite side is $3$ and the hypotenuse is $5$, so $\sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{5}$.
Dividing gives $3 \div 5 = 0.6$, so the value of $\sin\theta$ is $0.6$.

alternativeExplanations.title: The hypotenuse never changes; the others do
steps: The hypotenuse is always the side across from the right angle, regardless of which acute angle you are working with.
But "opposite" and "adjacent" swap when you switch from one acute angle to the other.
Label the triangle relative to the named angle *before* choosing a ratio.
